case: EXT-D-0120 same-run process attribution journal repair
root_cause: The guard emitted processes or unavailable, but the resource journal allowlist removed both properties before fsync and publication.
repair: The journal now persists exactly one validated attribution outcome: sanitized pid, parentPid, cpuPercent and executable accounting name rows, or unavailable:true. Unknown nested fields and raw error text are discarded. Malformed or path-like rows fail the journal write.
red_proof: Before the source change, node --test --test-name-pattern='process attribution survives journal publication' scripts/test-stabilization-resource-journal.mjs failed because the published attribution event lacked processes.
local_verification: After repair, node --test scripts/test-stabilization-resource-journal.mjs scripts/test-stabilization-resource-safety.mjs tests/browser/native-resource-boundary.test.mjs passed 15/15. The saved-journal test covers success, unavailable, ordering after unsafe, private field removal and invalid payload refusal.
prior_exact_commit_ci: https://github.com/armanisadeghi/matrx-extend/actions/runs/37204481673 ran the macOS disk integration without skip and failed at assert(Array.isArray(attribution.processes)) on e2a7cb96. Current repair needs a fresh exact-commit CI result.
fidelity_limits: macOS ps ucomm is an accounting name that may truncate. ps %cpu is a decaying average, not the guard's preceding iostat interval. The rows suggest likely CPU consumers but cannot prove exact interval ownership.
scope: No native browser run, heavy guard run, release or new CI was launched in this lane.
